results.summary: This Wokwi design uses an AND gate to drive a seven-segment LED display so that it shows the digit seven. It is controlled by two input switches, and the documentation says toggling inputs 3 and 4 causes the seven to appear. The project is a minimal educational logic example with very little documentation beyond the test instruction. It is a simple demonstration of combinational logic controlling a display.

This Wokwi project implements a full adder using three input switches for A, B, and Carry-in. The outputs drive LEDs to show the sum and carry-out. It is an educational example of combinational arithmetic logic. The design is simple and intended for learning digital logic.

This project is a numerically controlled oscillator (NCO) with a DAC output, capable of generating frequencies up to about 12.3 MHz. It is controlled via a parallel interface and includes a filter-analog block. The design is a compact signal-generation experiment with detailed pin-level control but no silicon test results. It is intended for audio or waveform generation applications.

This Wokwi project implements an 8-bit linear-feedback shift register that acts as a pseudo-random number generator. It uses a shift-register structure with feedback to produce a sequence of random-looking bits. The output is displayed on LEDs, and the design is controlled by switches. It is a simple educational example of LFSR-based PRNG.

This Wokwi project is a simple logic gate demonstration using LEDs and switches. It is designed for educational purposes to show basic digital logic. The project includes a Wokwi implementation with LED outputs. It is a minimal example of combinational logic.

This Wokwi project demonstrates flip-flop and multiplexer logic using LEDs and switches. It is an educational example of sequential and combinational logic. The design is implemented in Wokwi and uses LED outputs. It is a simple learning tool for digital circuits.

This project is an unmodified Tiny Tapeout Wokwi template with placeholder text such as 'testing 1 2 3' and instructions to explain how the project works. It is a boilerplate template intended for educational use. The design is incomplete and serves as a starting point for new projects. It includes basic LED output.

This Wokwi project is a Tiny Tapeout template used to test an LED digit display. It is a minimal display experiment rather than a defined function. The design uses a seven-segment display and LEDs. It is an educational example of driving a display.

This Wokwi design outputs a number on a seven-segment display corresponding to which input switch is high, so switch 0 shows 1, switch 2 shows 2, and so on. It is controlled by dip switches and uses a decoder to map the switch input to the display. The project is described as the author's first Wokwi design and is a simple educational switch-to-display exercise.

This project is a simple educational logic example with very little documentation. It uses a seven-segment display and LEDs to show a digit based on switch inputs. The design is implemented in Wokwi and is intended for learning purposes. It is a minimal demonstration of combinational logic.
